set.summary: Khalil al-Wazir (Abu Jihad), deputy to PLO chairman Yasser Arafat and a senior organiser of the intifada, was shot dead at his home in Tunis by Israeli commandos; two of his bodyguards and the household's gardener were also killed. The UN Security Council, in Resolution 611 of 25 April 1988, described the raid at Sidi Bou Said as an act of aggression against Tunisia. set.summary: During the Gulf War, Iraq fired 39 Scud missiles at Israel between 18 January and late February 1991, mainly at Tel Aviv and Haifa, aiming to draw Israel into the war and split the US-led coalition. Residents sheltered in sealed rooms with gas masks; two people died in direct hits and, counting suffocation in gas masks and heart attacks, 74 deaths were attributed to the attacks. At US request Israel did not retaliate. Israel placed the 1.7 million Palestinians of the West Bank and Gaza under a blanket curfew lasting about a month, which Human Rights Watch called the most severe collective punishment of the occupation to that date.

set.summary: Following Hezbollah rocket fire on northern Israel, the IDF launched a 17-day air and artillery campaign in Lebanon (11–27 April); Human Rights Watch writes that, as in 1993, its warnings were designed in part to displace upwards of 400,000 Lebanese civilians. On 18 April Israeli shells struck the UNIFIL Fijian battalion compound at Qana, where about 800 civilians sheltered, killing more than 100. A UN military adviser found it unlikely that the shelling resulted from technical or procedural error; the IDF attributed it to operational mistakes. Over the whole operation HRW counted some 154 Lebanese civilians killed and 351 injured; Hezbollah fired 639 Katyusha rockets into Israel, injuring 62 Israeli civilians and killing none (IDF figures). It ended with the Israel–Lebanon Ceasefire Understanding of 26 April.

The deportees camped on a hilltop near the border through much of 1993 while Israel and Lebanon each obstructed aid; Israel's Supreme Court upheld the deportations in January 1993, and under US and UN pressure Rabin announced on 1 February that 100 could return immediately and the rest in stages. Deportees including Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi and Mahmoud al-Zahar later led Hamas.

set.summary: Israel ('Roaring Lion') and the United States ('Epic Fury') launched large-scale strikes on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and senior commanders; his son Mojtaba Khamenei succeeded him. Iran fired about 650 ballistic missiles at Israel by early April, more than half with cluster warheads, struck US bases and Gulf states, and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. By early April Iranian missiles had killed 20 civilians and foreign nationals in Israel and four Palestinians in the West Bank, injured more than 7,000 people in Israel and displaced more than 5,500 Israelis; 13 US service members were killed. In Iran, estimates quoted by Reuters put the dead at over 3,600, of whom HRANA documented 1,701 civilians (the IDF claimed some 5,000 Iranian soldiers killed), and UNHCR estimated about 3.2 million people temporarily displaced. A two-week US-Iran ceasefire began on 7-8 April and a Pakistan-mediated interim memorandum followed on 14 June, but as of October 2026 there was no durable settlement.
